question: What is the penalty for using the ISI mark without a licence?

changed.sentence: Cognizable Offence: The offence under this sub-section is cognizable .

answer:
**Short answer**: Using the ISI mark (Standard Mark) without a licence is a contravention of Section 17 of the BIS Act, 2016, punishable under Section 29(3) with imprisonment up to two years, or a fine of at least ₹2 lakh (first offence) or ₹5 lakh (subsequent offences), or both, with the fine potentially extending up to ten times the value of the goods [1].

**Details**:
*   **Legal Basis**: The penalty is specified in Section 29(3) of the Bureau of Indian Standards Act, 2016, which applies to any person who contravenes the provisions of Section 17 [1].
*   **Imprisonment**: The term of imprisonment may extend up to two years [1].
*   **Fine Amounts**:
    *   For the **first contravention**, the fine shall not be less than **₹2 lakh** [1].
    *   For the **second and subsequent contraventions**, the fine shall not be less than **₹5 lakh** [1].
    *   The fine may extend up to **ten times the value** of the goods or articles produced, sold, or offered to be sold, or affixed/applied with the Standard Mark [1].
*   **Valuation Presumption**: If the value of the goods cannot be determined, it is presumed that one year's production was in contravention, and the annual turnover in the previous financial year is taken as the value of the goods for calculating the penalty [1].
*   **Cognizable Offence**: The offence under this sub-section is cognizable [1].

**Official links**:
*   BIS website: https://www.bis.gov.in

**Sources:**
[1] Bureau of Indian Standards Act, 2016: CHAPTER V > Section 29(3) Penalty for contravention, p. 14, dated 2016-03-22 | https://www.bis.gov.in/wp-content/uploads/2020/12/BIS-Act-2016.pdf#page=14
expected: Section 29(3) of the BIS Act, 2016: contravening Section 17 is punishable with imprisonment up to two years, or fine of not less than two lakh rupees for the first contravention and not less than five lakh rupees for subsequent contraventions, which may extend up to ten times the value of goods, or both.

question: What is the application fee for a BIS product certification licence?

changed.sentence: Under the BIS (Conformity Assessment) Regulations, 2018, the application fee, renewal application fee, and annual licence fee are rupees one thousand each .

answer:
**Short answer**: The application fee for a BIS product certification licence is Rs. 1000 [1][2].

**Details**:
- The application is required to be submitted along with an application fee of Rs. 1000 [1].
- Under the BIS (Conformity Assessment) Regulations, 2018, the application fee, renewal application fee, and annual licence fee are rupees one thousand each [2].

**Sources:**
[1] Product Certification FAQ: Frequently Asked Questions | https://www.bis.gov.in/product-certification/product-certification-faq/?lang=en
[2] BIS (Conformity Assessment) Regulations, 2018: Schedule - II > Scheme-I, p. 243, dated 2018 | https://www.bis.gov.in/wp-content/uploads/2019/03/BIS_CA_12032019.pdf#page=243
expected: Rs. 1000 application fee; an inspection fee of Rs. 7,000 per man day is paid before the preliminary inspection; after the decision to grant, an annual licence fee of Rs. 1000 plus the minimum marking fee for the product.

question: My licence validity has already expired. Can I still renew it?

changed.sentence: If you do not submit the application within this 90-day period, the licence shall stand expired and cannot be renewed .
Deferred Renewal Period: If you have not submitted the renewal application by the validity date, the decision to renew can be deferred for a maximum of 90 days from the date of validity .

Consequence of Missing Deadline: If the renewal application with the requisite fee (including the late fee) is not received within 90 days, the licence stands expired after the last date of its validity .
Restrictions During Deferral: You have no right to mark and dispatch the product with the Standard Mark after the date of validity .
Timeline: Within 90 days from the last date of validity .
If you miss the 90-day window: The licence stands expired .
If you mark products after expiry: You are not authorised to claim or supply material with the Standard Mark .

answer:
**Short answer**: Yes, you can still renew your licence if it has expired, provided you submit the renewal application within **90 days** from the last date of validity. You must pay the requisite fee along with a **late fee of Rs. 5,000** [1]. If you do not submit the application within this 90-day period, the licence shall stand expired and cannot be renewed [1].

**Details**:
*   **Deferred Renewal Period**: If you have not submitted the renewal application by the validity date, the decision to renew can be deferred for a maximum of **90 days** from the date of validity [1].
*   **Late Fee**: During this 90-day window, you may submit the renewal application form with the requisite fee and an additional late fee of **Rs. 5,000** [1].
*   **Consequence of Missing Deadline**: If the renewal application with the requisite fee (including the late fee) is not received within 90 days, the licence stands expired after the last date of its validity [1].
*   **Restrictions During Deferral**: You have no right to mark and dispatch the product with the Standard Mark after the date of validity [1].

**Step-by-step**:
1. Check the last date of validity of your licence.
2. Ensure you are within **90 days** from that date.
3. Prepare the renewal application form.
4. Pay the requisite renewal fee plus the **late fee of Rs. 5,000**.
5. Submit the application via Manak Online.

**Documents, fees and timelines**:
*   **Fee**: Requisite renewal fee + Late fee of Rs. 5,000 [1].

**What happens if...**:
*   **If you mark products after expiry**: You are not authorised to claim or supply material with the Standard Mark [1].

**Official links**:
*   Manak Online (apply for / manage a licence): https://www.manakonline.in/

**Sources:**
[1] Guidelines for Renewal of Licence: 2., p. 1, dated 2025-03-05 | https://www.bis.gov.in/wp-content/uploads/2025/03/RenewalGuidelines-WebsiteHosting.pdf#page=1
expected: Yes, within 90 days after the validity date, by paying an additional late fee of ₹5,000; the decision to renew may be deferred for up to 90 days from the validity date.

question: Is BIS certification compulsory for Sulphate Resisting Portland Cement?
answer:
**Short answer**: Yes, BIS certification is compulsory for Sulphate Resisting Portland Cement under Scheme I (ISI mark) [1].

**Details**:
*   **Product**: Sulphate Resisting Portland Cement [1].
*   **Standard**: IS 12330 [1].
*   **Scheme**: Scheme I (ISI mark), which applies to products under compulsory certification [1].
*   **Regulatory Basis**: The product falls under the Cement (Quality Control) Order, 2003 S.O. No. 191(E) Dt. 17 Feb 2003 [1].

**Sources:**
[1] Scheme I (ISI mark): products under compulsory certification: IS 12330: Sulphate Resisting Portland Cement | https://www.bis.gov.in/product-certification/products-under-compulsory-certification/scheme-1/?lang=en
expected: Yes, IS 12330 under Scheme I (ISI mark), Cement (Quality Control) Order, 2003, S.O. 191(E) dated 17 Feb 2003.

question: Is BIS certification compulsory for LED lamps? Which IS number and which QCO?
answer:
**Short answer**: Yes, BIS certification (specifically CRS registration under Scheme II) is compulsory for Self-Ballasted LED Lamps for General Lighting Services. The applicable standard is IS 16102 (Part 1) and the governing order is the Electronics and Information Technology Goods (Requirement of Compulsory Registration) Order, 2021, as amended by S.O.1246 (E) dated 10 March, 2026.

**Details**:
*   **Product**: Self-Ballasted LED Lamps for General Lighting Services.
*   **Scheme**: Scheme II (CRS registration).
*   **Standard**: IS 16102 (Part 1), titled "Self-Ballasted LED Lamps for General Lighting Services Part 1 Safety Requirements" [1].
*   **Regulatory Order**: The requirement is currently governed by the Electronics and Information Technology Goods (Requirement of Compulsory Registration) Order, 2021, which superseded earlier orders such as the 2012 Order and S.O. 2578(E) [1]. The latest amendments are per S.O.1246 (E) dated 10 March, 2026 [1].

**Official links**:
*   CRS registration portal: https://www.crsbis.in/BIS/registration-page.do
*   BIS website: https://www.bis.gov.in

**Sources:**
[1] Scheme II (CRS registration) page: IS 16102(Part 1): Self-Ballasted LED Lamps for General Lighting Services | https://www.bis.gov.in/product-certification/products-under-compulsory-certification/scheme-ii-registration-scheme/?lang=en
expected: Yes, self-ballasted LED lamps, IS 16102 (Part 1), under Scheme II (Compulsory Registration Scheme), Electronics & IT Goods (Requirements for Compulsory Registration) Order.

question: Do electronic control gears for LED modules need CRS registration?
answer:
**Short answer**: Yes, DC or AC supplied electronic control gears for LED modules require Scheme II (CRS registration) under the relevant Quality Control Order [1].

**Details**:
- **Product**: DC or AC Supplied Electronic Control gear for LED Modules [1].
- **Scheme**: Scheme II (CRS registration) [1].
- **Governing Orders**: Originally covered under the Electronics & Information Technology Goods (Requirements for Compulsory Registration) Order, 2012 (Notification No. S.O. 2905(E) dated 07 November 2014), subsequent amendments, and superseded by the Electronics and Information Technology Goods (Requirement of Compulsory Registration) Order, 2021 along with its later amendments (such as S.O. 1246(E) dated 10 March 2026) [1].

**Official links**:
- BIS website: https://www.bis.gov.in [1]

**Sources:**
[1] Scheme II (CRS registration) page: IS 15885 (Part 2/Sec 13): DC or AC Supplied Electronic Control gear for LED Modules | https://www.bis.gov.in/product-certification/products-under-compulsory-certification/scheme-ii-registration-scheme/?lang=en

question: बिना लाइसेंस के ISI मार्क लगाने पर क्या सज़ा है?
answer:
**Short answer**: बिना लाइसेंस या कंट्रावेंशन (Section 17 के उल्लंघन) के ISI मार्क का उपयोग करने पर BIS अधिनियम, 2016 की धारा 29(3) के तहत सज़ा का प्रावधान है [1]।

**Details**: 
धारा 17 के उल्लंघन (जैसे बिना लाइसेंस के सामान पर स्टैंडर्ड मार्क लगाना या बेचना) के मामले में निम्नलिखित दंड दिए जा सकते हैं [1]:
- पहली बार उल्लंघन करने पर दो साल तक की कैद या कम से कम दो लाख रुपये का जुर्माना, या दोनों हो सकते हैं [1]।
- दूसरे और उसके बाद के उल्लंघनों के लिए पांच लाख रुपये से कम न होने वाला जुर्माना या कैद, या दोनों हो सकते हैं [1]।
- यह जुर्माना उत्पादित, बेचे गए या ऑफर किए गए सामान के मूल्य के दस गुना तक बढ़ाया जा सकता है [1]।
- यदि सामान का मूल्य निर्धारित नहीं किया जा सकता है, तो एक साल के उत्पादन को उल्लंघन में माना जाएगा और पिछले वित्त वर्ष के वार्षिक टर्नओवर को सामान का मूल्य माना जाएगा [1]।
- धारा 29(3) के तहत अपराध संज्ञेय (cognizable) है [1]।

**Official links**:
- BIS website: https://www.bis.gov.in [Official Links]
- BIS CARE app (verify licence or complaint): https://play.google.com/store/apps/details?id=com.bis.bisapp [Official Links]

**स्रोत:**
[1] Bureau of Indian Standards Act, 2016: CHAPTER V > Section 29(3) Penalty for contravention, p. 14, dated 2016-03-22 | https://www.bis.gov.in/wp-content/uploads/2020/12/BIS-Act-2016.pdf#page=14
expected: Section 29(3): imprisonment up to two years, fine at least 2 lakh (first) / 5 lakh (subsequent), up to ten times value of goods.
